persistence_invariants.brief: Unique composite key on (sku, location) so no two rows share the same SKU-at-location pair; a repeat filing collides and updates in place (R3).
sku, location, and quantity are NOT NULL so a filed record always carries its identity and level.
CHECK quantity >= 0 so a stored stock level can never go below zero (R2).

The Alembic migration creating stock_records is reversible: upgrade re-creates the table with its full schema (columns plus the PI1 unique, PI2 NOT NULL, and PI3 CHECK constraints) and downgrade cleanly drops it. Because this migration first creates the table, the round-trip guarantee is schema-recreation (table and its constraints are present after upgrade), NOT row survival across the drop (R1).

nfrs.brief: The schema migration is reversible against the real branch. Because this initial migration CREATES stock_records, its round-trip test asserts schema-recreation (after upgrade the table and its PI1/PI2/PI3 constraints exist) and a clean downgrade that drops the table, NOT row survival across the create-table round-trip (a downgrade drops the table, so row-survival is unsatisfiable here). Row-preservation applies only to later purely-additive migrations over an existing table.
Stock levels never persist below zero; a filing that would drive quantity negative is rejected at write time (CHECK constraint PI3 plus service-layer guard).
Every (sku, location) pair is uniquely addressable; collisions resolve to an in-place update at write time via the DB unique constraint PI1 (never two duplicates, never an error page).

Integration tests run against the paired Lakebase branch (databricks_postgres via DATABASE_URL), never a mock or in-memory substitute; CI refuses a PR whose integration tests do not run against a real branch.

The boundary is a JSON API returning data (not server-rendered HTML); the UI is a React + TypeScript SPA under client/ that navigates client-side and updates rows in place. The API is covered by the R4 branch integration tests.

Validation failures on filing return clear, specific messages that name the offending field (not a bare 'bad request'). Owned at the API boundary (app/routes/), applied before any persistence. REQUIRES a real-branch behavior test (kind: behavior) that POSTs an invalid filing payload (e.g. a missing/blank required field such as the tracking code or SKU) to the boundary and asserts the HTTP response body carries a message identifying the specific failing field — distinct from the negative-quantity guard (NFR-F1-2/AC3), which names the quantity field. (PO preference.)

The home stock table renders cleanly across the populated and empty paths: the React SPA (client/) shows one row per record with the quantity column right-aligned, and shows an explicit empty-state message (never a blank page or a null crash) when the API returns no records. Owned by the client presentation layer over the JSON boundary (R5). Covered by client component tests plus the R4 branch integration test on the boundary's collection response. (PO preference: a view missing optional/zero-record detail still renders cleanly.)
